title: Making Money
text: “Gua!”
“It grew this big in just one night? Monsters are amazing, aren’t they?”
The next morning, my Father looked up at Kuro-chan with a look of surprise. Kuro-chan is currently in his second form—the standard Filolial form.
“Well then, Kuro-chan, go fight the nearby monsters with Father and gain some real-world combat experience.”
“Gua!”
“Um, how do you form a party? Oh, is this it…? So that woman intended to deceive me from the very beginning…”

Muttering things like that, Father sent a party formation request to Kuro-chan. A permission request to add Kuro-chan to my party popped up in my field of vision. This is the master’s approval via the Monster Crest. Without hesitation, I granted permission, and my Father and Kuro-chan completed their party formation.
“Kuro-chan, take Father on your back and go fight.”
“Gua!”
“Just hop on? Got it.”
Kuro-chan crouched down, and Father climbed onto his back.
“Well then, Father. Please come back safely.”
“U-uh-huh. Thank you for everything, Motoyasu-kun.”
“Not at all. Well then, have a safe trip!”
When I waved to Kuro-chan, she cheerfully set off, carrying my father on her back.
“Whoa! So fast, so fast—”

In the blink of an eye, my father was riding on Kuro-chan’s back and galloping away. Well then… what should I do next? I’ve gathered a decent amount of materials, but my funds are a bit tight. Before I went back in time, I didn’t have any particular worries, but I have a major goal now. That is to reunite with Filo-tan. And if I’m lucky, I might even become Filo-tan’s master.
“All right!”

That day, I decided what I was going to do. I’m going to make some money. If going to the guild doesn’t work out, I’ll sell the materials I’ve gathered for money. If I still need more money than that, I’ll hunt down some thieves and rob them. That’s something my Father used to do all the time. And so, I returned to the town below the castle and made my way to the Adventurers’ Guild.
“I’m truly sorry, but we cannot arrange any work for the Spear Hero.”

When I spoke to the male clerk at the Adventurers’ Guild reception desk, that was his reply. Without a word, I pointed my spear forward, put all my strength into it, and asked in a threatening tone as sparks flew from the blade.
“Don’t say that—isn’t there any job that’ll pay?”
“Oink!”
A pig standing behind the clerk let out some kind of squeal. How noisy. Should I take it out? I show no mercy to pigs. Don’t get too big for your boots, you lowly livestock.
“N-no matter what happens, the kingdom has not granted permission.”
“…That’s… um, Aultcray’s order, right? And Bitch… no, wait. Is the princess in on this too?”
The male clerk kept averting his gaze while repeatedly urging me to leave. He’s probably being threatened by those Trash guys.
“If the queen of this country heard about this… I wonder how she’d respond?”
“Ugh…”

As I was grilling him, a pig holding a letter approached from behind and handed it to the clerk. He’s likely a member of the group known as “The Shadows.” I can’t fully trust these guys, but they were on my Father’s side. I can’t treat them lightly.
“…Yes. Understood. Just as the Spear Hero said. Please, this way.”
“I’d prefer the option that pays the most and saves the most time. It’d be best if there’s an advance payment.”
“T-this way.”

And so, I accepted a job from the Adventurers’ Guild—with an advance payment, of course. So, I’ll be getting a little money. It was a relief that my Father had mentioned that the Crimson Swine’s mother was a decent person. I didn’t really understand what they were talking about, but she was supposedly a decent pig who said she’d overlook my sins as long as I fought for the world. As expected, mentioning the Queen’s name does make things a bit more flexible. I’ll just keep saying “Queen, Queen” from now on.
“‘Spear Hero! Prepare yourself!’”
Just as I stepped out of the Adventurers’ Guild, several adventurers surrounded me and charged.
“Windmill!”
“““Gwaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaah!?”””

Without a moment’s hesitation, I unleashed my area-of-effect skill, Windmill. This is a skill where I swing my spear sideways to create a tornado. In Ren’s case, it’s a spinning slash-like motion. For me, it’s a skill where I swing my spear around like a baton.
“What’s with this sudden attack? If you keep messing around, I’ll kill you.”
I’m not going to hold back against these flying sparks. They’re probably just some Trash assassins anyway.
“Guh… You fake hero, siding with the Demon of the Shield!”
…That phrase sounds familiar. Ah! The Three Heroes Church, right? I see—so that faction is still active.
That shitty religion my Father led to ruin. Wasn’t it the state religion of this country? I’m a bit fuzzy on the details. I’d completely forgotten.
“Fake Hero? Never heard of him. I am The Love Hunter, who lives for love. If you’re out to get my Father, shall I storm the Three Heroes Church right now and slaughter every last one of you?”
I press the tip of my spear against the adventurer’s cheek and smile. A scourge that torments my Father… What should I do about it?
“Ah, a demon… You demon!”

“I don’t think it’s acceptable to humiliate my Father—the Shield Hero—with baseless accusations. This is a warning. If you harm us, I’ll eliminate you without hesitation. You’d better be prepared. Hahahahaha!”
With that, I walked away, laughing loudly. Of course, I’ve taken the wallets of those foolish fanatics who attacked me. With this, I can buy a new Filolial-sama.
“Die! You devil!”

I can hear the howls of these nobodies. I couldn’t care less. Next, I’ll take the materials to a random buyer. Of course, I made sure they bought them from me while threatening to kill them if they tried to act disrespectful.
Jingling my money pouch, I made my way to the slave trader’s tent. The slave trader was wiping sweat from his brow with a hand towel.
“W-what would you like this time? Another Filolial? Yes?”
“That’s right. Next time, I’d like several of them.”

Come to think of it, there’s no need to limit myself to just one angel at a time. So I plan to allocate every spare coin I have toward purchasing Filolials. Of course, it goes without saying that I’ll set aside money for Father’s equipment. It’d also be nice to bring back materials from various monsters.
“H-here you go.”
The slave trader showed me a box filled with eggs once again. I picked out a few from it and bought them.
Well then, there’s still plenty to do! I quickly wrapped up the quest from the Adventurers’ Guild. Before I knew it, the sun had set.
“Ah, Motoyasu. Welcome back.”
When I returned to the village, my Father and Kuro-chan were waiting for me.
“How did it go?”
“I’ve managed to raise a decent amount of money as well.”
I showed my Father the money pouch.
“W-wow, that’s amazing.”

Of course, since I spent some money along the way, it isn’t that much, but I earned a huge amount just by defeating nearby monsters—a task the Guild says is difficult to accomplish. Back when we didn’t know how to level up, this was a Level 70 quest, but with my current strength, it was a piece of cake. Even dragons don’t scare me.
“We’ll use this as a stepping stone to train Filolial-sama even further.”
I showed my Father a Filolial egg as a souvenir. I bought a lot of them, so he seemed surprised by the quantity.
“Kua?”
Kuro-chan tilted his head.
“How far along are you now, Father?”
“Um… I’m Level 15 now.”
“That’s quite a pace.”

“Though it was mostly just Kuro-chan knocking monsters aside as he went. Also… it seems like Kuro-chan is getting a little bigger bit by bit. The one we saw at the castle was already fully grown, right?”
Father pets Kuro-chan. Kuro-chan, in turn, narrows his eyes happily. It’s a heartwarming sight. My Father always used to look at Filo-tan with those same eyes. I’m pretty sure of it.
“Kua!”
“That’s right. I think he’ll start speaking by tomorrow evening.”
“Huh… Filo-real can talk!?”
“That’s right. Filolial-sama is a truly wonderful Filolial-sama.”
“Huh… I’m looking forward to it. There aren’t any talking animals in my original world, so it’s kind of magical. That’s what you’d expect from another world.”
That day, too, Father treated us to a home-cooked meal.
And then, the next morning. I spotted Father talking to someone in front of the inn’s counter.
“Ah, Motoyasu-kun.”
“Is something wrong?”
Father spotted me and called out.
“You see, these folks are asking me to bring you here. Do you think you might know who they’re looking for, Motoyasu-kun?”
Two pigs and one man… I turned my gaze toward the man. He looked like a Demi-Human, with wolf-like ears.
“I… am an envoy from Siltvelt. I take it you are the Spear Hero. Would you be so kind as to hear us out?”
